item.text: {"classifications":[{"segment_id":"1","code":0,"rationale":"This is a historical recital describing a determination made in Proclamation 10339; it neither directs a current actor nor itself creates a present legal consequence.","evidence":"In Proclamation 10339, I determined that the safeguard action on imports of CSPV cells"},{"segment_id":"2","code":0,"rationale":"This segment recounts the earlier extension, statutory reporting requirements, the USITC report, and an industry petition; it contains no new presidential command or present legal act.","evidence":"I further determined to extend the safeguard measure proclaimed in Proclamation 9693"},{"segment_id":"3","code":3,"rationale":"The President presently makes the statutory positive-adjustment determination that supports modification of the safeguard action; the legally consequential determination occurs in this segment itself.","evidence":"I have determined that the domestic industry has been making and is continuing to make a positive adjustment to import competition"},{"segment_id":"4","code":3,"rationale":"The President determines and specifies the expansion of the tariff-rate quota to 12.5 GW, while the segment itself also establishes how the annual in-quota quantity is allocated; the trade-law consequences arise from the presidential act itself.","evidence":"by expanding the TRQ to unchanging within-quota quantities of 12.5 GW"},{"segment_id":"5","code":3,"rationale":"The President directly modifies the HTS, establishes its effective period, and exempts qualifying imports up to the new 12.5 GW limit from safeguard tariffs; these legal consequences occur by operation of the proclamation.","evidence":"subchapter III of chapter 99 of the HTS is modified as set forth in Annex I to this proclamation"},{"segment_id":"6","code":4,"rationale":"The segment inseparably combines an implementation direction to CBP with self-executing future deletion of tariff provisions and immediate supersession of inconsistent prior directives, so it contains materially different legal postures.","evidence":"U.S. Customs and Border Protection shall take such actions as are necessary to ensure proper application"}]}
